subject: music
topicDisplay: Areas Of Inquiry Music For Listening And Performance
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In African music, the 'master drummer' typically...?
options: Sets up the instruments before the performance
Leads the ensemble, signalling changes and improvising over the cyclic patterns
questions.explain: The master drummer leads, cues changes and improvises over the underlying cyclic patterns.

questions.q: In strict four-part writing, which is a forbidden parallel motion?
questions.explain: Consecutive (parallel) perfect fifths and octaves are prohibited in traditional voice-leading.

questions.q: Gamelan ensembles commonly use which two tuning systems?
questions.explain: Gamelan typically uses the five-note slendro and the seven-note pelog tuning systems.

questions.q: The Argentine 'tango' is most associated with which instrument providing its characteristic sound?
questions.explain: The bandoneón, a button accordion, gives the tango its distinctive timbre.

questions.q: The 'jhalla', the closing section of a North Indian raga performance, is characterised by...?
options: A return to the opening alap
Silence with only the drone sounding
A fast, exciting climax with rapid rhythmic strumming
A slow, free and unmetred mood
questions.explain: The jhalla is the fast, rhythmically exciting climax that ends the performance.

questions.q: A passing note is which type of non-chord tone?
options: Approached by leap and left by step
Approached and left by step in the same direction filling a melodic gap
A note that returns to its starting pitch
A sustained dissonance held over a barline
questions.explain: A passing note connects two chord tones a third apart, approached and quitted by step in the same direction.

questions.q: A 'reel', another Celtic dance type, is usually in...?
options: Simple quadruple time (4/4 or cut common) with a flowing quaver movement
questions.explain: The reel is a fast dance in simple quadruple time with continuous even quavers.

questions.q: A modulation from C major to G major is a move to which related key?
questions.explain: G major is the dominant key of C major, a closely related key with one extra sharp.

questions.q: The dominant of A minor, when used to create a perfect cadence, normally contains which note as its third?
questions.explain: In the harmonic minor the leading note is raised, so E major (the dominant of A minor) contains G sharp.

questions.q: A plagal cadence consists of which progression?
questions.explain: The plagal ('Amen') cadence moves from the subdominant (IV) to the tonic (I).

questions.q: In a major key, which chord built on the dominant typically functions as the dominant seventh?
options: A diminished seventh chord on the leading note
A major-minor (dominant) seventh chord on scale degree 5
A minor seventh chord on the supertonic
A major seventh chord on the tonic
questions.explain: The dominant seventh is a major-minor seventh chord built on the fifth degree, comprising a major triad plus a minor seventh.

questions.q: 'Call and response' is a texture common in African (and African-American) music in which...?
options: Two unrelated melodies are played simultaneously
The music has no fixed pulse
A leader's phrase (call) is answered by a group (response)
All voices sing exactly the same line throughout
questions.explain: In call and response a soloist's call is answered by the group's response, an antiphonal texture.

questions.q: In Indian classical music the term 'bol' refers to...?
options: Mnemonic syllables used to represent and recite drum strokes or rhythms
questions.explain: Bols are spoken mnemonic syllables representing tabla strokes and rhythmic patterns.

questions.q: The interval from C up to G is which?
questions.explain: C up to G spans seven semitones, a perfect fifth.

questions.q: The relative minor of G major is which key?
questions.explain: The relative minor shares the key signature of G major (one sharp) and is E minor.

questions.q: The Indonesian 'gamelan' is primarily an ensemble of...?
questions.explain: A gamelan is built chiefly from tuned metallophones, gongs and drums.

questions.q: In an Indian classical ensemble, which pairing of instruments is most typical?
questions.explain: The sitar plays the melody while the tabla provides the rhythmic accompaniment.

questions.q: In ensemble performance, good 'ensemble skills' include all of the following EXCEPT...?
options: Watching for cues and breathing together
Maintaining a shared sense of pulse
Listening and balancing dynamics with other players
Deliberately ignoring the other performers' tempo
questions.explain: Strong ensemble playing depends on listening, balancing and keeping together, not ignoring fellow performers.

questions.q: Which mode results from playing the white notes from D to D?
questions.explain: The Dorian mode runs from D to D on the white notes, with a minor third but a major sixth.

questions.q: What characterises a cadential six-four chord?
options: A second-inversion tonic chord on a strong beat resolving to V before the cadence
A tonic chord in root position resolving to V
A dominant chord in third inversion
questions.explain: The cadential 6/4 is a second-inversion tonic chord on an accented beat that delays and decorates the dominant before the cadence.

questions.q: In performance, 'interpretation' refers to...?
options: Transposing the music to a new key
Playing the notes exactly as printed with no expressive choices
The performer's expressive choices of dynamics, phrasing, tempo and articulation within the score
questions.explain: Interpretation is the performer's expressive shaping of dynamics, phrasing, tempo and articulation.

questions.q: In figured bass, the symbols '6/4' indicate which inversion of a triad?
questions.explain: A 6/4 figure denotes a second-inversion triad, with the fifth in the bass.

questions.q: A secondary dominant such as V of V in C major would be which chord?
questions.explain: In C major, the dominant is G, and the dominant of G (V of V) is a D major chord.

questions.q: Augmentation as a melodic device involves which alteration?
options: Restating a theme with proportionally lengthened note values
Transposing a theme up an octave
Restating a theme with shortened note values
questions.explain: Augmentation lengthens the rhythmic values of a theme, typically doubling their duration.

questions.q: An interrupted cadence most commonly progresses from which chord to which?
questions.explain: An interrupted (deceptive) cadence moves from V to vi, thwarting the expected resolution to the tonic.

questions.q: An atonal passage is best characterised by which feature?
options: Strict adherence to a major scale
A clear tonic and dominant relationship
The absence of a tonal centre or key
questions.explain: Atonality avoids any sense of a key or tonal centre, abandoning functional harmony.

questions.q: A Picardy third refers to which feature?
options: A third added above the melody
A minor-key piece ending on a major (raised third) tonic chord
A chord built on the third degree
A major piece ending on the minor third
questions.explain: A tierce de Picardie raises the third of the final tonic chord so a minor-key work ends on a major chord.

questions.q: In the alap–jhor–jhalla–gat structure, the 'gat' section is distinguished by...?
options: The entry of the tabla and a fixed, composed melody with a regular tala
A solo drone with no melody
A return to the unmetred opening
questions.explain: The gat is the composed, metred section where the tabla enters and a fixed melody is set within a tala.

questions.q: A homophonic texture is characterised by which?
options: Two or more independent equal melodic lines
A melody supported by chordal accompaniment
questions.explain: Homophony features a principal melody accompanied by chords, all parts moving largely together.

questions.q: A German augmented sixth chord contains which intervals above the bass?
options: Major third, augmented fourth and augmented sixth
Major third, perfect fifth and augmented sixth
Major third and augmented sixth only
questions.explain: The German sixth comprises a major third, perfect fifth and augmented sixth above the bass note.
